The ‘cost-of-living squeeze’ mediates survival of Sceloporus occidentalis
text:
Welcome to the analytical and computational documentation for our study investigating how thermal environment and energetic demands—the cost-of-living squeeze (COLS)—influence the survival and spatial ecology of western fence lizards (Sceloporus occidentalis) across elevation gradients.
This repository is structured as a reproducible research website containing the complete workflows, statistical analyses, spatial models, and biophysical simulations supporting the manuscript.

title: The ‘cost-of-living squeeze’ mediates survival of Sceloporus occidentalis
text:
Vignettes and Analyses
Each document in this repository addresses a specific component of the study:

home-range-estimation.qmd
Processes mark-recapture data, evaluates capture saturation and sampling completeness across field seasons, estimates empirical inter-annual survival rates, and delineates individual Minimum Convex Polygon (MCP) home ranges across high- and low-elevation populations.
resting-metabolic-rates.qmd
Analyzes resting metabolic rates (RMR) across temperatures, body sizes, and populations to parameterize temperature-dependent energetic expenditure functions.
feeding-demand.qmd
Translates thermal and metabolic costs into daily and seasonal feeding demands, quantifying the intensity of the cost-of-living squeeze experienced by individuals.
cols-survival.qmd
Tests the direct and interactive effects of metabolic feeding demands (COLS) on individual survival probabilities and population demographic rates.
simulations-behavioral-thermoregulation.qmd
Implements biophysical and behavioral thermoregulation simulations to model operative environmental temperatures, activity windows, and thermoregulatory costs under current and projected thermal landscapes.

title: The ‘cost-of-living squeeze’ mediates survival of Sceloporus occidentalis
text:
Datasets Included
The repository includes raw and processed data stored within the data directory:

data/mr_data.rds
The compiled longitudinal mark-recapture dataset. Contains individual identities (id), capture dates (year, doy), sex, morphometric traits (snout-vent length svl, mass), and geographic coordinates (lat, lon, utm_x, utm_y).
data/home_ranges.rds
Derived spatial polygon vertices computed via convex hulls (chull) for individuals with \(\ge 4\) relocations after removing spatial outlier records (\(> 150\text{ m}\) from individual centroids). Used for comparative spatial extent analysis across elevations.
